daily.title: HEG Ltd lists at 25% premium, hits lower circuit

On the NSE, the stock opened at ₹587, up ₹118.75, or 25.36 per cent, from the pre-listing value of ₹468.25. On the BSE, it listed at ₹580, a 24.99 per cent premium to ₹464.05.

daily.title: Customs: Penalties on customs broker set aside where no knowledge of export overvaluation shown - CESTAT New Delhi
daily.summary: CESTAT New Delhi sets aside penalties on a customs broker, ruling no knowledge of export overvaluation was proven. Learn more about this significant ruling. Brief : A customs broker filed export shipping bills for an exporter whose goods were later found overvalued, and penalties under sections 114(iii) and 114AA of the Customs Act, 1962 were imposed on the broker and upheld by the Commissioner (Appeals). The Tribunal held that the Revenue had brought no evidence that the broker knew of the overvaluation, and no proceedings had been initiated against the broker under the Customs Brokers Licensing Regulations, 2018.

Why is RBI bringing its gold back to India? The big shift decoded
breaking.summary: Gold prices may be falling, but central banks around the world are continuing to buy gold. This unusual trend highlights the growing importance of gold as a safe-haven asset amid global economic uncertainty and changing financial strategies.At the same time, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is bringing more of India's gold reserves back to the country. While global central banks are increasing their gold holdings, India is also strengthening control over its gold reserves, reflecting a significant shift in the global financial landscape.

breaking.title: RBI eases daily CRR maintenance to 90% from 99% as liquidity tightens
breaking.summary: Banking system liquidity has swung from a surplus of Rs 11.16 lakh crore in September to a deficit in November, prompting the central bank to restore flexibility in banks' daily reserve management. The liquidity deficit widened to Rs 47,641.20 crore on November 26 from Rs 32,216 crore a day earlier, according to RBI data. The weighted average call rate (WACR) stood at 5.76 percent on November 27, above the RBI's marginal standing facility (MSF) rate of 5.75 percent. The pressure was also evident in the central bank's liquidity operations on November 27.

breaking.title: SEBI allows FPIs to trade in physically settled commodity derivatives, puts in place risk safeguards
breaking.summary: The circular will come into effect from June 1, 2027, giving market infrastructure institutions time to put the necessary systems and operational arrangements in place. Market regulator SEBI has allowed foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to participate in physically settled non-agricultural commodity derivatives, a move aimed at deepening institutional participation and improving market liquidity. The relaxation comes with a risk-management framework to ensure that foreign investors exit their positions before the delivery period begins. Under the revised framework, FPIs can trade in non-agricultural commodity derivative contracts, except options in goods, and indices comprising such derivatives.

breaking.title: India’s forex reserves fall by $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion, RBI data shows
breaking.summary: India's forex reserves fell $4.44 billion to $700.90 billion in the week ended November 20, with gold reserves declining by $4.10 billion. In the previous week, the overall kitty had dropped by USD 14.205 billion to USD 705.342 billion. The reserves had touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion during the week ended September 4, driven by a heavy flow of currency as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record USD 133 billion, but have been on a decline ever since.
